title: TFOP verdicts to 2026 support a TESS multiplicity boost above 5 only below 6 Earth radii, and verdicts from 2020 over-stated the later false-positive fraction 1.2 to 5.7 times
abstract: Question: Do two common reliability inputs for TESS planet candidates (TOIs) agree with later follow-up verdicts? The inputs are the multiplicity boost of Guerrero et al. (2021) (B = 20, or 54 below 6 Earth radii), and the false-positive (FP) fraction among TOIs that already have a verdict. Method: We froze 4,671 TOIs on 2020-11-20 (an Internet Archive copy of the ExoFOP table) or at alert from 2020-11-21 to 2022-12-31. We compared them with the TFOP verdicts of 2026-11-09. We estimated B as the FP odds ratio of single-candidate to multi-candidate hosts, with an exact conditional likelihood in strata of cohort, pipeline, radius and period. We compared the FP fraction of the verdicts available in 2020 with the later verdicts on the TOIs that were open in 2020. Results: Below 6 Earth radii, 0 of 122 verdicts on multi-candidate TOIs are FP, against 6.4 expected with no boost (p = 0.0002). This gives B > 5.5 (95%), and B = 20 and B = 54 both agree with the data. The result holds with planets that have a dynamical mass (B > 5.8), with a strict multiplicity definition, and in each cohort. At 6 Earth radii or more, 4 of 7 multi-candidate verdicts are FP (B = 1.4, range 0.25-8.0). The data reject B = 20 (p = 0.004) and B = 54 (p = 0.0002), but only three host systems give this result. On 2020-11-20, 88% of 622 verdicts were FP. Later verdicts on the TOIs then open were 40% FP (278 of 700). In seven stratification schemes, the 2020 verdicts over-state later FPs 4.1-5.7 times for SPOC 2-minute TOIs and 1.23-1.32 times for QLP TOIs (p < 1e-15). For SPOC TOIs below 6 Earth radii, the FP fraction changed from 73% to 7%. With Gaia DR3 RUWE and crowding in the strata, the SPOC factor stays at 3.7 and the QLP factor falls to 1.03. Latent-class competing-risks models fitted to the 2020 snapshot alone did not forecast the 2026 verdicts. Thus one snapshot cannot correct this verdict-timing bias. Limitations: There are only 4 multi-candidate FPs. Some planet verdicts come from validations that used a boost. 101 small multi-candidate TOIs are still open, and 3 new FPs among them would lower the estimate to B = 4. TFOP dispositions are heterogeneous. Job sci-1107-hp-astronomy-9243866ab9c7, model claude-opus-5-5.
